mergedParams.userDescription: Words sliding smoothly into place, one after another, in a clean line. typo kinetics for titles/captions/other text..

output.title: Smooth Sliding Text Animation - Clean Typokinetics

prompts.prompt: Create a typokinetics preset where words slide in sequentially from the right edge of the screen, decelerating smoothly into their final positions like a video editor pulling clips into a timeline. Each word should arrive with a subtle bounce-ease that mimics professional motion graphics. Think of it as if you're keyframing text layers in After Effects - each word is a separate layer that slides in with custom timing. The words should form a single clean horizontal line, with precise spacing that feels editorial and intentional. Add a subtle motion blur effect during the slide motion (using CSS blur filter during transform) that clears as each word settles, similar to motion blur in video rendering. The animation should feel like watching a well-edited title sequence where text elements smoothly cascade into place.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'flex flex-row items-center justify-center gap-2' for horizontal word alignment. Each word should be a TextAtom wrapped in its own BaseLayout with 'relative' positioning. Implement slide animation using generic effects with translateX from '100%' to '0%' over 0.4s per word with 'ease-out' easing. Add staggered delays using relative timing - each word starts 0.15s after the previous. Apply motion blur using filter effect transitioning from 'blur(2px)' to 'blur(0px)' synchronized with the translate animation. Use containerProps.className for the main container and childrenProps for individual word containers. Consider using an internal effect preset for the slide-blur combination that can be reused. Set will-change: transform, filter on animated elements for GPU acceleration.

prompts.prompt: Design a minimal, elegant typokinetics preset inspired by clean documentary title cards. Words fade in sequentially while simultaneously sliding up from below their baseline, creating a subtle lifting effect like text emerging from fog. Think of this as layering text with a soft vertical wipe transition in your NLE - each word reveals itself through both opacity and position. The timing should be deliberate and measured, like a thoughtful editor placing each word with intention. Keep the motion understated - only 20-30 pixels of vertical travel. The final result should feel like premium streaming platform titles where less is more. Add a slight scale animation (0.95 to 1) to give dimensionality without being flashy.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using 'inline-flex flex-wrap items-baseline' to maintain natural text flow. Each word as TextAtom with BaseLayout wrapper using 'inline-block overflow-hidden' for clipping. Create compound effect using AnimationRange arrays: opacity 0 to 1, translateY from '30px' to '0px', scale from 0.95 to 1, all with 'ease-in-out' over 0.6s. Stagger each word by 0.08s using relative timing calculations. Use containerProps.style for line-height control. Consider implementing as a typography preset that accepts caption data for automatic word-level timing. Add 'transform-gpu' class for hardware acceleration. Set up fitDurationTo: 'children' to auto-calculate total duration.

prompts.prompt: Build a dynamic typokinetics preset that mimics the feel of kinetic typography in music videos - words slide in from alternating directions (left/right) creating a zigzag flow of energy. Imagine cutting between different text angles in Premiere Pro, but smoothly animated. Each word should have a quick snap-in motion with a strong ease-out curve, like a whip-pan transition. Add a subtle rotation during the slide (5-10 degrees) that straightens out as the word locks into place, similar to handheld camera stabilization. The words ultimately align in a clean horizontal line, but the journey there should feel energetic and rhythmic. Include a brief overshoot on the position before settling, like elastic easing in motion graphics.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'flex flex-row items-center justify-center gap-3 w-full'. Implement alternating logic in presetExecution to determine slide direction (even index from left, odd from right). Apply effects array with: translateX alternating between '-120%' and '120%' to '0%', rotate from alternating '10deg' and '-10deg' to '0deg', with custom spring easing over 0.5s. Add overshoot by keyframing to '5%' or '-5%' at 80% progress, then to '0%' at 100%. Use childrenProps with conditional className based on index. Consider using helper functions for alternating logic. Enable GPU compositing with 'will-change-transform' and 'transform-3d'. Implement as a caption-based typography preset for automatic word extraction.

prompts.prompt: Create a sophisticated typokinetics preset inspired by high-end fashion brand videos where words glide in with liquid smoothness. Think of this as using bezier curves in your animation timeline - perfectly smooth acceleration and deceleration. Words should slide horizontally but with a subtle wave motion, as if they're floating on water. Each word arrives with a different speed based on its length (shorter words move faster, longer words more deliberately), like varying clip speeds in your edit. Add a subtle brightness pulse as each word settles, similar to a luma key effect. The overall feeling should be luxurious and fluid, with timing that breathes rather than rushes.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using 'flex flex-row items-center gap-4 px-8'. Calculate animation duration based on word length: base 0.8s + (0.05s * character count). Implement wave motion using compound transform: translateX from '150%' to '0%' with cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1), translateY using sine wave calculation (Math.sin for 3 keyframes). Add brightness pulse using filter effect: brightness from 1 to 1.3 to 1 over the last 30% of animation. Use presetExecution to calculate per-word timings. Store word length calculations in helper function. Apply 'antialiased' and 'subpixel-antialiased' classes for smooth text rendering. Consider backdrop-filter for premium feel if background present.

prompts.prompt: Develop a punchy, attention-grabbing typokinetics preset that feels like quick-cut editing in an action movie trailer. Words slam into place with impact, sliding in fast then hitting an abrupt stop with a tiny shake, like a crash zoom effect. Think of each word as a separate shot that cuts in with kinetic energy. Add a brief scale pop (1.0 to 1.1 to 1.0) on arrival for emphasis, similar to impact frames in animation. Include a subtle shadow that slides in slightly behind each word, creating depth like a drop shadow effect in post. The timing should be aggressive and rhythmic, with shorter gaps between words to maintain momentum.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'flex flex-row items-center justify-center gap-2 font-bold'. Implement rapid slide with translateX from '200%' to '0%' over 0.25s using 'cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)' for abrupt stop. Add shake effect at end: 2 rapid translateX oscillations between '-2px' and '2px' over 0.1s. Scale pop using scale keyframes: 1 to 1.1 at 90%, back to 1 at 100%. Create shadow with ::after pseudo-element or duplicate TextAtom with 'absolute -z-10 opacity-30' positioning, offset by translate(-2px, 2px). Stagger timing aggressively at 0.05s intervals. Use transform-origin: center for scale. Apply will-change: transform for all animated properties.

prompts.prompt: Design an organic, flowing typokinetics preset where words appear to be written by an invisible hand, sliding in with a natural handwriting rhythm. Imagine tracking text across frames in your video editor, but with the smoothness of calligraphy. Each word should slide in with varying speeds that mimic the cadence of writing - function words (the, and, is) move quickly, while content words take more time. Add a subtle opacity fade that trails the slide, like ink flowing onto paper. Include slight vertical variations in final position (±2-3px) to avoid perfect alignment, maintaining a human touch. The effect should feel like watching time-lapse calligraphy.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Build with BaseLayout using 'flex flex-row flex-wrap items-center gap-2'. Categorize words in presetExecution: function words at 0.3s, content words at 0.5s duration. Implement slide with translateX from '100%' to '0%' with custom easing per word type. Add opacity gradient using clip-path or mask-image with linear-gradient animation. Apply random vertical offset using transform: translateY with Math.random() * 6 - 3 pixels. Stagger delays based on cumulative word timing for natural rhythm. Use caption metadata if available to identify word importance. Consider letter-spacing animation for added fluidity. Store word categorization logic in helper function.

prompts.prompt: Create a grid-based typokinetics preset inspired by terminal/code interfaces where words slide in like command-line text, but arranged in a clean horizontal line. Think of it as if you're editing a tech/hacker scene - each word types itself into existence through a slide-reveal effect. Use a monospace aesthetic but with smooth motion instead of choppy typing. Words should slide in with a subtle glitch effect midway through (brief position jitter), like digital interference. Add a faint glow that pulses once as each word locks in, similar to a terminal cursor. The timing should be precise and mechanical, with exact intervals between words.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using 'flex flex-row items-center font-mono gap-4 bg-black text-green-400'. Implement slide using translateX from '100%' to '0%' over 0.4s with linear easing for mechanical feel. Add glitch at 50% progress: rapid translateX and translateY jitter (±3px) for 0.05s using multiple keyframes. Create glow effect with text-shadow animation: from 'none' to '0 0 10px currentColor' to 'none' over last 20% of animation. Use exact 0.1s stagger between words. Apply 'tracking-wider' for monospace feel. Consider adding scanline effect with CSS gradient overlay. Use transform: translate3d for GPU acceleration during glitch.

prompts.prompt: Build a perspective-based typokinetics preset where words slide in from a vanishing point, creating depth like a Star Wars opening crawl but horizontal. Imagine using 3D camera moves in After Effects - words start small and far away, then slide forward growing to full size. Each word should maintain perspective during the slide, with those at the edges having more dramatic angles. Add a subtle blur-to-focus effect that simulates depth of field. The final line should feel like text floating in 3D space that has gracefully assembled itself. Include slight rotation on the Y-axis during approach for added dimensionality.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'flex flex-row items-center justify-center gap-3 perspective-1000'. Apply 3D transforms per word: translateZ from '-300px' to '0px', scale from 0.5 to 1, rotateY from '25deg' to '0deg' for edge words, less for center. Implement depth blur with filter: blur transitioning from '3px' to '0px' synchronized with translateZ. Calculate rotation based on word position relative to center using index. Stagger from center outward for symmetric reveal. Use transform-style: preserve-3d on container. Apply backface-visibility: hidden for performance. Consider using CSS custom properties for dynamic perspective values.

prompts.prompt: Design a bouncy, playful typokinetics preset inspired by cartoon motion graphics where words slide in with exaggerated physics. Think of this like animating with squash-and-stretch principles in your video editing - words compress slightly on arrival then bounce back to shape. Each word slides in on a slight arc (not straight line), like tossing objects into place. Add a rotation wobble during flight (rotating back and forth), settling to zero on landing. Include a brief squash effect on impact (scaleY compression) before returning to normal. The animation should feel like a Pixar title sequence - fun but professionally crafted.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using 'flex flex-row items-center justify-center gap-3'. Create arc motion using cubic-bezier path: combine translateX from '150%' to '0%' with translateY parabola (use 3-4 keyframes for arc). Add rotation wobble: animate rotate between '-15deg' and '15deg' during flight, settling to '0deg'. Implement squash on landing: scaleY to 0.85 at 85% progress, then spring back to 1. Use spring easing or cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55) for bounce. Stagger each word by 0.12s with slight overlap for energy. Apply transform-origin: bottom center for squash effect. Consider adding subtle skew during flight for extra personality.

prompts.prompt: Create a cinematic typokinetics preset with words sliding in like film credits, but horizontally instead of vertically. Imagine the precision of end credits in a Christopher Nolan film - perfectly timed, weighted, and dramatic. Words should slide in with a slow build-up, accelerate through the middle, then ease into position with gravitas. Add a subtle letter-spacing animation that contracts as words settle, like text compressing into focus. Include a brief fade on the leading edge during slide for a softer entry. The overall effect should feel epic and deliberate, suitable for important titles or dramatic captions.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'flex flex-row items-center justify-center gap-4 text-4xl font-light'. Implement slide with translateX from '120%' to '0%' over 1.2s using cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0, 1) for cinematic acceleration. Animate letter-spacing from '0.2em' to '0em' over same duration for compression effect. Add edge fade using mask-image with linear-gradient, animating mask-position. Use longer stagger of 0.2s between words for weight. Apply 'uppercase tracking-wide' for cinematic style. Consider adding subtle brightness animation from 0.8 to 1 for fade-in feel. Use will-change: transform, letter-spacing for optimization. Structure as typography preset to leverage caption data for dramatic word emphasis.
